per_policy_guidance.guidance: Validated reliability: 12/12 from this policy’s own nominal training-segment entry states. Every run ended with enough poured (12 particles in the bowl), the container upright and at the return region, one gripper-command change, and zero IK-unconverged steps; formal success was first reached at steps 301–409. Use with `source_object="container", destination="target_pose"` after pouring, while the source is securely held and upright or nearly upright. Its destination-frame action prior makes it the documented choice when target displacement is the main concern after righting, but displacement itself was not validated, so do not treat that benefit as measured. Avoid a substantially tilted/unusual handoff, unreliable target observation, an unreachable target, grasp loss, or any need for collision/contact/release recovery. Detect failure through IK non-convergence or limit contact, source/TCP separation, premature opening, an elevated or moving source after opening, or failure to become upright and remain in the return region. Replan every eight actions. If entry remains strongly tilted or otherwise unusual, the documented switch is h02; near nominal setdown when release timing dominates, switch to h03. This is terminal: hand off only to evaluation after observing upright stationary support in bounds, open fingers, and clear TCP retreat (documented near 0.28 m); there is no successor manipulation policy.

Validated reliability: 12/12 from its nominal segment entries. All runs finished with enough poured (12 particles), an upright container at the return region, one gripper-command change, and no IK-unconverged steps; first formal success occurred at steps 291–517. Invoke as `source_object="container", destination="target_pose"` when the emptied container is still securely grasped and the handoff is at the demonstrated moderate tilt, upright outbound, or another feasible intermediate phase. The fresh-TCP body-increment representation is the documented preference when predecessor timing/state mismatch is the main concern, but no out-of-distribution intermediate-state test was performed. Avoid use after grasp loss, with infeasible IK, or as evidence of recovery from collision, failed support, or premature release; it has no constructed destination-displacement equivariance. Failure signs are repeated IK failures, large or oscillating local commands, absent target progress, source/TCP separation, opening before low upright support, source motion after release, or retreat recontact. Replan every eight actions and decode each slot from fresh measured TCP/joints rather than accumulated predictions. Once upright, the documented handoff is h01 if target displacement dominates; near nominal support, use h03 if release timing dominates. Terminal completion requires physically observed upright stationary placement in bounds, open fingers, and TCP clearance, then hand off to evaluation.

Validated reliability: 12/12 at its nominal training-segment entries. Every run ended with enough poured (12 particles), the container upright and at return, one gripper-command change, and zero IK-unconverged steps; first formal success was at steps 292–405. Call with `source_object="container", destination="target_pose"`. Prefer it when the securely held, upright container is near the nominal demonstrated return support or descending and setdown/open/retreat phase ambiguity is the main issue. Its output is absolute world-frame and its auxiliary head only regularizes learned phase; neither target displacement nor auxiliary-contact accuracy was validated. Avoid displaced-goal cases, strongly tilted/off-trajectory handoffs, and any use of auxiliary logits as a release gate, contact signal, or success test. Recognize failure by opening while elevated, tilted, moving, or outside return bounds; remaining closed after stable setdown; source movement after opening; retreat recontact; IK non-convergence; or limit contact. Continue causal replanning through setdown, opening, and upward retreat. The documented switch is h01 for a displaced target and h02 for a strongly tilted/unusual intermediate state. This policy is terminal; hand off to evaluation only from physical observations of upright stationary support in bounds, open fingers, and clear TCP retreat, not from an auxiliary prediction.

Observed reliability is poor: only 3/12 nominal in-distribution runs passed. All nine failures ended with the container outside the return region; four also ended non-upright and had 360–394 IK-unconverged steps, while the other five remained upright but still missed return. Failed runs showed 3–74 gripper-command changes versus one in each passing run. Therefore no reliably validated selection niche was identified, and this policy should not be the default when h01–h03 are available. Its intended source-frame niche—an accurately observed, securely grasped source with off-cluster source pose or source/TCP relation—is only a documented hypothesis; there is no out-of-distribution validation. If used experimentally, call `source_object="container", destination="target_pose"`, monitor every eight-action replan, and stop/switch on source/TCP separation, motion inconsistent with a closed-finger grasp, oscillating source-relative targets, no destination progress, repeated IK failure/limit contact, premature opening, post-release source motion, or retreat recontact; never chase a lost/free source. The documented switches are h02 when the source anchor is questionable and fresh-TCP correction is safer, h01 after righting when destination displacement dominates, and h03 near nominal support when release phase dominates. Even a transient success is insufficient: terminal handoff to evaluation requires observed upright stationary in-bounds support, open fingers, and TCP clearance.

summary: Validation replayed each policy from the entry state of its own training segment in each of 12 training demonstrations, ran it for 1.5× segment length, and scored final-state task success (enough poured, container at return, upright). This is strictly in-distribution evidence; no displaced-target, altered-handoff, recovery, or other out-of-distribution result exists. h01, h02, and h03 each passed 12/12, always ending with 12 particles in the bowl, an upright returned container, one gripper-command change, and no IK-unconverged steps. Validation does not establish a reliability ranking among those three; choose by the documented prior: h02 for secure tilted/intermediate handoff, h01 after righting when destination-relative transport is desired, and h03 near nominal support when release phase is the concern. Those special-case benefits remain unmeasured outside the nominal entries. h04 passed only 3/12 and should be treated as experimental rather than a production default. Common prerequisites are that pouring is complete and the source is still securely grasped. No policy has demonstrated recovery from slip, collision, failed support, premature release, regrasp, or corrective repouring. Completion is terminal: rely on physical observations—not predictions or transient success—of upright stationary placement in the return region, open fingers, and clear TCP retreat before handing off to evaluation.
